doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Brubeck's solos and the Tonight Show band with Ernie Watts
summary: Brubeck added saxophone solos for him, then he toured with Doc Severinsen's Tonight Show band and traded solos with Ernie Watts.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: sudden he falls in love. Now the next time he comes back to Buffalo there’s four saxophone solos that he’s put in there because he knows I’m here. And he’s asking for me. Now he takes me out to do a couple of other orchestra dates with him, in other cities, and then asked me if I wanted to do the Tonight Show band when they take it on the road. I said yeah, hell yes. And I get to go out on the road, on a bus, and hang out with Conte Candoli, Snooky Young, you know, all the cats. The real deal. I mean these cats have been doing it for ages. They’ve got stories, I mean just ridiculous, just ridiculously fun hang, and the second time I go out, who’s playing the other tenor chair is Ernie Watts. And I’m like I transcribed your stuff, and I’ve got tunes that you wrote that I’ve done out when you were with Bruce and doing all that stuff and everything else. So we started playing. And Doc of course, he’s got two shooters here. So he’s going to give us a tune where the two of us blow and blow off each other. And we do that thing, and it was so out, I automatically, because of my ears, I will try and cop the style of what I hear. He does the same thing, he’s copping me. And I’ve never heard anybody do it. I’ve never heard anybody do that. It was so funny it was great. So that was a major—
Well gosh have you ever had anything that went terribly bad?
That’s good. All that preparation paid off.
